evals.name: summarize-session-logs
evals.prompt: I need to understand what happened in my recent session logs — specifically Session-270 through Session-274. They're in my Obsidian vault at /Users/sunginkim/GIT3/ArkNode-AI/vault/Trading-Signal-AI/Session-Logs/. For each session, tell me: the topic (from the title or heading), the status, and the tags. Don't dump the full content — just a concise summary of each.
evals.expected_output: A concise summary of 5 sessions with topic, status, and tags for each. Should NOT contain full file contents.

assertions.name: used_cli_or_minimal_reads
assertions.description: Agent used obsidian CLI commands (outline, properties, search) OR read files with minimal context, rather than reading 5 full session files

assertions.name: all_sessions_covered
assertions.description: Output mentions all 5 sessions (270-274) with topic/status info

assertions.name: concise_output
assertions.description: Final output is under 2000 characters — agent didn't dump raw file contents

evals.name: create-obsidian-note
evals.prompt: Create a new research note called 'Benchmark-Analysis' in my Obsidian vault at /Users/sunginkim/GIT3/ArkNode-AI/vault/Trading-Signal-AI/Research/. It should have: proper YAML frontmatter with tags (research, analysis, benchmark), status: draft, date: 2026-03-06. In the body include wikilinks to [[Session-274]] and [[Session-273]], a tip callout with placeholder text, and a mermaid flowchart showing Input -> Processing -> Output. Use proper Obsidian markdown syntax.
evals.expected_output: A new .md file created with valid Obsidian frontmatter, wikilinks, callout, and mermaid diagram

assertions.name: used_cli_create
assertions.description: Agent used 'obsidian create' CLI command rather than the Write tool to create the file

assertions.name: valid_frontmatter
assertions.description: File has valid YAML frontmatter with tags, status, and date

assertions.name: obsidian_syntax
assertions.description: File uses proper Obsidian syntax: wikilinks ([[...]]), callout (> [!tip]), mermaid block

evals.name: query-base-data
evals.prompt: I want to see data from my Sessions.base in my Obsidian vault. The base file is at Trading-Signal-AI/Session-Logs/Sessions.base. Show me all sessions that have 'complete' status. Format the results nicely.
evals.expected_output: Structured table/list of sessions with complete status, pulled from the base view

assertions.name: used_base_query
assertions.description: Agent used 'obsidian base:query' CLI command rather than reading the .base YAML file directly

assertions.name: shows_complete_sessions
assertions.description: Output shows sessions with complete/completed status

assertions.name: structured_output
assertions.description: Results are presented in a structured format (table or organized list)

evals.name: task-management
evals.prompt: Show me all the tasks in my Obsidian vault at /Users/sunginkim/GIT3/ArkNode-AI/vault — I want to see what's on my plate. Group them by status if possible. Then create a new task called 'Benchmark Obsidian Skills' with project trading-signal-ai, priority high, and status todo.
evals.expected_output: List of tasks grouped by status, plus a new task file created with proper TaskNotes frontmatter

assertions.name: used_cli_for_listing
assertions.description: Agent used 'obsidian tasks' or 'obsidian base:query' to list tasks rather than globbing and reading individual files

assertions.name: used_cli_for_creation
assertions.description: Agent used 'obsidian create' with proper frontmatter rather than Write tool

assertions.name: task_created_correctly
assertions.description: New task has proper frontmatter: task-id, status: todo, priority: high, project: trading-signal-ai, tags: [task]

evals.name: vault-health-check
evals.prompt: Run a full health check on my Obsidian vault at /Users/sunginkim/GIT3/ArkNode-AI/vault. I want to know: how many broken links, orphan notes, dead-end notes, total files, and give me the top 10 most-used tags with counts.
evals.expected_output: Vault health report with counts for broken links, orphans, dead ends, total files, and top tags

assertions.name: used_cli_commands
assertions.description: Agent used obsidian CLI commands (unresolved, orphans, deadends, files, tags) rather than manual file scanning

assertions.name: all_metrics_reported
assertions.description: Output includes counts for: broken links, orphans, dead ends, total files, and top tags

assertions.name: efficient_execution
assertions.description: Health check completed in 5 or fewer tool calls

evals.name: create-canvas
evals.prompt: Create a canvas file at /Users/sunginkim/GIT3/ArkNode-AI/vault/Trading-Signal-AI/Strategy-Overview.canvas showing a flowchart of the trading pipeline: 'Signal Generation' (green) connects to 'Position Manager' (yellow) which connects to 'Execution Engine' (red). Each node should have a brief description. Add labeled edges between them.
evals.expected_output: Valid JSON Canvas file with 3 colored text nodes and 2 labeled edges forming a left-to-right flowchart

assertions.name: valid_json_canvas
assertions.description: File is valid JSON with 'nodes' and 'edges' arrays

assertions.name: correct_node_colors
assertions.description: Nodes use correct color presets: green (4), yellow/orange (2 or 3), red (1)

assertions.name: proper_edges
assertions.description: 2 edges connecting the 3 nodes in sequence with labels

evals.name: web-extract-summarize
evals.prompt: I want to understand Obsidian's Bases syntax. Extract the content from https://help.obsidian.md/bases/syntax and give me a summary of the key features and filter syntax.
evals.expected_output: Clean summary of Bases syntax covering filters, views, formulas, and properties

assertions.name: used_defuddle
assertions.description: Agent used 'defuddle parse --md' rather than WebFetch to extract page content

assertions.name: covers_key_features
assertions.description: Summary covers filters, views, formulas, and/or properties

assertions.name: not_raw_html
assertions.description: Output does not contain raw HTML tags or navigation elements
